sentences.text: Kryptohadros is a monotypic genus, known only from a partial skull and skeleton belonging to the species Kryptohadros kallaiae.
The holotype was recovered between 2022 and 2024 at the Fântânele-3 locality in Hunedoara County, Romania.
János Magyar and his team formally introduced the genus and species in a 2026 publication.
The generic name merges Greek terms for “hidden” and “bulky,” reflecting its previously unnoticed hadrosauroid status in the Hațeg Basin.
The specific epithet honors Csilla Kállai, the mother of the describer.
Bone growth indicators show that the holotype individual had attained at least a subadult stage.
Phylogenetic studies place Kryptohadros within the endemic Telmatosauridae clade, alongside Telmatosaurus and Tethyshadros.
Thus it is assigned to the broader family Telmatosauridae.
The animal lived in the Maastrichtian interval, roughly 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
It represents the second named non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroid discovered from the Hațeg Basin.
